subject: Dedicated capacity sizing / hot-standby and slotting plan
messages:
From: Claire Johnson <claire@aegis-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Ben Cooper <ben.cooper@aegis-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity questionnaire and target throughput

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking our RFI — attached is the questionnaire from procurement (we included the traffic samples and representative prompt set). High-level ask: we plan to move a mix of user-facing chat and inference jobs to a dedicated pool and want guidance on a reservation that supports 2,000 steady qps (peak 2,800 qps spikes), 95th pct latency budget 180ms for generation up to 1k tokens, and strong tail guarantees. Models planned: custom fine-tuned LLMs derived from open-family 70B (quantized); KV cache hit expected ~40%.

Key constraints:
- Must be able to provide hot-standby for DR during a regional outage (cross-region fallback).
- Procurement timeline: PO target by 2028-06-15.
- We need an outline of recommended GPU SKUs (incl. H100 vs A800 tradeoffs), projected throughput per-SKU for this workload, and a suggested reservation + burst strategy.

Attached: aegis_rfi_gpu_profile.xlsx (traffic samples + prompt profiles).

Could you turn around a sizing recommendation and provisional MAP (mutual action plan) by next week? If useful we can schedule a two-hour workshop with our infra team.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Johnson
Sr. Procurement Manager | Aegis Analytics
procurement@aegis-analytics.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire and target throughput

Hi Claire — thanks, received the workbook. I've looped in Rishi (capacity lead) and Kimberly (contracts) to own sizing and procurement cadence.

Quick clarifying questions before we build the slotting scenarios:
- Is the 2,000 qps steady target an average over a 24h window or a weekday business-hours baseline?
- Do you expect synchronous chat (low concurrency per user) to dominate, or will you have large batching from async inference jobs?
- Any explicit requirement for max accepted p99 latency? You mentioned p95 at 180ms; helpful to confirm p99 target as that drives standby sizing.

We attached a short workbook template and will return a proposal with: GPU SKU mix recommendations, throughput per-SKU with assumed batch sizes, suggested reservation commit + burst lane sizing, and a hot-standby/DR approach.

I added a stub Drive folder for the exchange: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAegisRFI

Can you confirm a convenient time Thursday or Friday for a 60–90m sizing workshop?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Claire Johnson <claire@aegis-analytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire and target throughput — Redwood preliminary sizing

Claire — attaching our preliminary sizing and a short narrative (attached as redwood_reserve_pricing_v2.pdf). Highlights here to keep the thread actionable: 

Summary recommendation (steady-state, expected workload mix from your samples):
- Recommended baseline reservation: 6 x H100-80GB (fp16 / quantized path) + 4 x A800-80GB as cost efficient capacity for queued batch jobs.
- Expected steady throughput: ~2,100 qps aggregate with batching target of 6–8 tokens/batch for chat-style prompts (70B quantized, KV cache hit 40%).
- Tail capacity & headroom: reserve 10% of baseline as warm headroom; add a dedicated 2-node hot-standby in a secondary region for cross-region failover. That standby is kept warm with periodic health-check traffic and can accept scaled traffic within 30–90s depending on session KV warming.
- Latency projections (end-to-end generation): p50 ~90–120ms, p95 ~170–200ms (aligned with your 180ms threshold), p99 depends heavily on KV warming — projected ~300ms with cold cache.

Sizing notes: these numbers assume: quantized 8-bit execution path, average sequence length 400 tokens, batching policy that prioritizes latency SLOs with occasional aggressive batching for background jobs. If your workload skews to longer sequences or lower cache hit, we recommend +2 H100 equivalents.

Pricing & reservation guidance:
- Commit to baseline (6H100 + 4A800) for guaranteed throughput and preferential slotting.
- Add a small burst pool that can autoscale to +30% using on-demand capacity (pay-as-you-go) during launch weeks.

Next steps suggested:
1) Workshop to lock steady vs peak definitions and confirm p99 target (we propose Fri 10:30 PDT).
2) Run a 10-day soak on a pilot pool (2 H100 + 1 A800) to validate real KV hit and tail behavior.
3) Finalize reservation contract and PO milestones (we note your 2028-06-15 PO target).

Attachments: redwood_reserve_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing sketch + slotting options).

Let us know if you want a split SKU option that favors A800 for cost with H100 for strict latency-critical lanes.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Capacity & Product Strategy | Redwood Inference
From: Claire Johnson <claire@aegis-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Cooper <ben.cooper@aegis-analytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 08:14:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity questionnaire and target throughput — clarifications

Rishi / Soojin — thanks, this is helpful. A couple clarifications from procurement/infra: 

- The 2,000 qps steady target is our peak weekday business-hours baseline (14:00–20:00 UTC). Outside that window we expect ~40% lower steady.
- We require a p99 SLA for customer-facing chat of 400ms or better; we understand the difficulty with cold KV warming but need design patterns to meet this.
- Hot-standby: procurement requires a documented failover time and a brief runbook for session preservation (or how sessions degrade) during cutover.
- PO timeline is firm (2028-06-15). Could you include a documented acceptance criteria for the 10-day soak so procurement can sign off?

On the workshop: Friday 10:30 PDT works for us. Also please include an itemized slotting proposal and an example canary rollout plan in the MAP.

Thanks,
Claire

Claire — attaching a short MAP in the Drive folder and summarizing below so procurement has a clear path to PO: 

Mutual Action Plan (draft):
1) Workshop (Fri 10:30 PDT) — confirm p99 target (400ms) and business-hours window; agree on pilot traffic slices. Owner: Redwood (Rishi) / Aegis infra. Due: 2028-05-11.
2) Pilot & Soak — 10-day pilot (2 H100 + 1 A800) run by Aegis with Redwood telemetry access. Acceptance criteria: sustained baseline qps within ±10% of target, p95 ≤ 200ms, p99 ≤ 400ms for customer lane. Owner: Aegis infra / Redwood SE. Due: 2028-05-31.
3) Slotting & Reservation — final baseline reservation (recommended: 6 H100 + 4 A800) to be contractually reserved. Contract paperwork & PO by 2028-06-15. Owner: Aegis procurement / Redwood sales (Kimberly).
4) Canary rollout — phased rollout across customer cohorts; maintain a 10% warm headroom during first 14 days. Owner: Aegis product / Redwood support.
5) DR & Hot-standby — maintain cross-region hot-standby (2-node warm cluster) with documented failover runbook. Cutover target: under 120s session acceptance window; session degradation documented. Owner: Redwood reliability.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/HS-23456 — Kimberly, please attach final contract artifacts here when ready.

If that looks right we'll finalize the MAP and add the formal acceptance criteria to the pricing appendix for procurement sign-off.

Thanks — I'll follow up after the workshop with updated slotting spreadsheets.

Best,
Soojin
